correctness.rationale: The invariant antidiagonal yields the exact increasing recurrence \(u_{n+1}=u_n[1+2\varepsilon+a(u_n-1)e^{-u_n}]^2\). Centering at the unique large balance root, the scaled one-step increment converges uniformly on compact offsets to \(1+e^{-w}\), and its mesh tends to zero. A monotone comparison bounds pre-layer scaled time by \(e^{1-L}\). Sending the entrance cutoff \(L\) to infinity yields the softplus integral, then inversion gives the orbit profile. Root uniqueness, normalization and numerical consistency were checked, but the infinite theorem follows from analysis.

originality.rationale: The closest same-map theorem proves escape at the exact border \(b=1/2\) but not a positive-detuning joint first-passage limit. Another published claim already covers the subcritical antipodal two-cycles \(b<1/2\); that subject is expressly excluded. Full primary article and exact same-map prior proof were read and compared by quantifiers. The asymptotic \(\log(1+e^t)\) depends on coupling approaching the border as observation time diverges, a regime not implied by fixed-coupling escape existence or the known critical law. Unindexed equivalents remain a risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed or inaccessible general singular-perturbation first-passage theorem could imply this specific softplus limit.
General off-antidiagonal initial conditions are not treated; this deliberate restriction is a theorem scope, not an inferred full-plane conclusion.

value.rationale: The published Gaussian map has a distinguished unbounded-orbit threshold at \(b=1/2\). Existing exact work gives the critical escape law and the opposite-side antipodal cycle, leaving the natural finite-horizon question when \(b=1/2+\varepsilon\) and \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). The complete softplus curve quantifies both competing escape mechanisms on the physical delay scale \((\varepsilon\log(1/\varepsilon))^{-1}\), yielding a transferable benchmark for nearly critical transient observations. It is not a mere renaming, static threshold, or finite computation.
